stories.title: Alcaraz Survives Faria Scare, Advances to US Open R3 (TIER 1)

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text: "Tough match for me." — Alcaraz after dropping the first set to Faria before dominating the next three at #USOpen 2026. Now into R3 vs. Wu Yibing. The title defence is on. #Tennis

facebook.long_form:
Window: 8:00 AM ET

Carlos Alcaraz dropped the first set. Then he dropped five games in the second set. And then it was over.

The defending US Open champion recovered from a shaky opening to defeat Portugal's Jaime Faria 4-6, 6-0, 6-3, 6-2 in 2 hours and 40 minutes at Arthur Ashe Stadium on Thursday, advancing to the third round of the 2026 US Open.

Faria — ranked No. 72 — started well, serving solidly and breaking Alcaraz in the seventh game to build a 5-3 lead before closing out the first set with an ace. For a moment, it looked as if the defending champion might be in real trouble.

But the second set told a very different story. Alcaraz upped his pace, Faria's serve fell apart, and the Spaniard broke three times to take the set without losing a game. He then held his level through the third and fourth sets to move through comfortably.

"Tough match for me," Alcaraz said afterward. "Obviously the first set, I was feeling great, I had break point, I missed it." He acknowledged the difficulty of the opening frame but stayed composed when it mattered.

Alcaraz will face China's Wu Yibing in the third round. He is now two wins away from the quarterfinals. The title defence is very much alive.

stories.title: Tien Ends Monfils' Farewell — Emotional Goodbye at Louis Armstrong (TIER 1)

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text: Learner Tien eliminates Gael Monfils 6-3, 0-6, 6-3 to end his 18th and final #USOpen. After the last point, Tien walked to the net and asked Monfils to sign a ball. Perfect send-off. #Tennis

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text: Gael Monfils. 18 US Opens. 35 Grand Slam wins. A career like no other. The No. 1 entertainer in tennis history took his last bow at Louis Armstrong today. #USOpen #Tennis

facebook.long_form:
Window: 10:30 AM ET

Gael Monfils is done at the US Open. After 18 appearances, 35 match wins, and a career unlike any other, the 40-year-old Frenchman's Grand Slam journey ended Thursday at Louis Armstrong Stadium.

No. 14 seed Learner Tien defeated Monfils 6-3, 0-6, 6-3 in 121 minutes. Tien was composed, crafty, and clinical — everything the moment required against a player who had spent 20 years thrilling crowds at Flushing Meadows.

Monfils had arrived in New York for one final farewell. He had celebrated his 40th birthday just two days earlier with a vintage four-set win over Adolfo Daniel Vallejo, briefly becoming the oldest man to win a US Open match since Jimmy Connors in 1992. The crowd at Arthur Ashe had roared for him. The story was perfect.

Then Tien came along.

The 20-year-old American seized control in the first set, slipped through a bad patch in the second when Monfils levelled brilliantly (6-0), then steadied to take the third and the match.

What happened next may be the lasting image of this match. After the final point, Tien walked to the net — and asked Monfils to sign a ball for him. That moment, a 20-year-old honouring the legend he had just beaten, said everything about what Monfils meant to the sport.

Monfils will play Paris Masters later this season and then retire. He has given tennis more than most. Today was goodbye.

stories.title: Eala Faces Oliynykova in High-Stakes R2 Rematch (TIER 2)

x_posts.label: Post 3-1
x_posts.text: Alex Eala (No. 17) faces Oliynykova in US Open R2 today — a rematch of the Strasbourg R1 Oliynykova won 3-6, 7-5, 6-3. First hard-court meeting. Eala is in form. #USOpen #Tennis

x_posts.label: Post 3-2
x_posts.text: After a 6-1, 6-2 R1, No. 17 seed Alex Eala returns to Louis Armstrong Stadium for her biggest match — R2 vs. Oliynykova at #USOpen 2026. Philippines watching. #WTATennis

facebook.long_form:
Window: 12:30 PM ET

Alex Eala came to New York with unfinished business. On Thursday, she gets a chance to settle it.

The No. 17 seed and Philippine tennis trailblazer faces Ukraine's Oleksandra Oliynykova in the second round of the 2026 US Open at Louis Armstrong Stadium — a rematch of a match Eala lost in Strasbourg just months ago.

That Strasbourg clash, played in May 2026 on clay, ended 3-6, 7-5, 6-3 in Oliynykova's favour. Eala had the first set but couldn't close it out. It was the kind of loss that stays with a player.

Now they meet again — on hard court at Flushing Meadows, a surface Eala has made her own. She arrived at this US Open ranked No. 17, the highest Grand Slam seeding in Philippine tennis history, and backed it up immediately with a demolition of qualifier Mary Stoiana in the first round: 6-1, 6-2 in 78 minutes.

Oliynykova is no pushover. She defeated American wild card Reese Brantmeier 6-4, 6-4 in round one and leads the head-to-head 1-0. But this is a different surface and a different Eala from the one Oliynykova faced in Strasbourg. The Philippines is watching.

stories.title: Day 5 Evening Slate — Gauff, Zverev, Rybakina Headline Night Session (TIER 2)

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text: Thursday night at #USOpen: Gauff vs. Badosa (7 PM ET, Arthur Ashe), Zverev vs. Halys, Rybakina vs. Bouzas Maneiro. Three of the biggest stars left in the draw take the court. #Tennis

facebook.long_form:
Window: 6:00 PM ET

Thursday night at Flushing Meadows is exactly what the US Open was built for.

Three of the tournament's biggest names take the court in the evening session: No. 4 seed Coco Gauff faces No. 7-ranked Paula Badosa on Arthur Ashe at 7 PM ET; No. 1 seed Alexander Zverev plays France's Quentin Halys; and No. 2 seed Elena Rybakina — still managing questions about her Cincinnati ankle injury — takes on Spain's Jessica Bouzas Maneiro.

Gauff is the defending US Open champion, and Badosa is one of the most in-form players on tour. They've met before. Expect a battle on the biggest stage in tennis.

Zverev has yet to play his R2 match at these championships. As the top seed, Thursday is his first real opportunity to put down a statement. Halys is capable, but Zverev will be expected to handle him.

And Rybakina — who had been unable to walk without pain before this tournament — has already passed one test, beating Thea Frodin 6-3, 6-2 in round one with minimal sign of discomfort. Bouzas Maneiro is the next challenge.

Coverage starts at 7 PM ET on ESPN.

stories.title: US Open R3 Draw Picture — Alcaraz Leads as Big Three Gone (TIER 2)

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: US Open men's R3 forming: Alcaraz ✓, Tien ✓, Tsitsipas ✓. Still to play R2: Zverev, FAA, Fritz, de Minaur. Djokovic, Sinner, Fils all gone. This draw is wide open. #USOpen #Tennis

facebook.long_form:
Window: 3:00 PM ET

The 2026 US Open men's draw has lost its structure. Now it's chaos — and that means opportunity.

Jannik Sinner (knee) never arrived. Novak Djokovic fell in the first round to Navone on Day 1. Arthur Fils — the Cincinnati champion — was stunned by Stefanos Tsitsipas in round two. On Thursday, Gael Monfils lost his final US Open to No. 14 seed Learner Tien.

Meanwhile, Carlos Alcaraz is marching through. The defending champion handled Jaime Faria 4-6, 6-0, 6-3, 6-2 Thursday to reach the third round, where he meets China's Wu Yibing. Alcaraz looks like the player to beat.

But the rest of the draw is genuinely open. No. 1 seed Alexander Zverev plays Quentin Halys Thursday evening — his first real test at these championships after Djokovic's early exit removed the biggest threat from his half. Felix Auger-Aliassime (No. 3) faces Karen Khachanov. Taylor Fritz (No. 9) takes on Mattia Bellucci.

Tsitsipas — who shocked Fils — is in the third round. Tien is now there too. A draw without Sinner, Djokovic, and Fils is genuinely up for grabs.

Alcaraz believes. And right now, that belief is entirely justified.
